model_conventions.checked_scope: The current source-facing model proves the individual-accuracy formula from this event identity and embeds each finite adversarial witness as an exact joint PMF with unchanged classifier accuracies.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: A collaboration setting is represented by one probability law on X x {0,1}, rather than by an input marginal plus a selected pointwise conditional-label function. Predictors are measurable [0,1]-valued functions and calibration means, for every measurable A, E[1_{P_i(X) in A,Y=1}] = E[P_i(X) 1_{P_i(X) in A}].
model_conventions.unresolved_relation_to_literal_source: User-approved formalization convention: the paper's calibration display is read through this event-calibration semantics. The report records that this does not select a pointwise conditional version on every arbitrary input space.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source writes conditioning on P_i(X)=p for every reported p, but a raw joint law does not canonically specify conditional probabilities on zero-probability prediction fibers. The event identity is meaningful for both atomic and atomless prediction laws.

model_conventions.checked_scope: The raw reliability predicate carries the strategy-expectation well-formedness premise; the source proof's finite witnesses discharge it directly.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: Predictors are measurable, and a strategy is used in an accuracy comparison only when its induced binary-correctness indicator is integrable under the joint law. On finite witnesses this condition is automatic.
model_conventions.unresolved_relation_to_literal_source: This is an analytic well-formedness convention, not a claim that every set-theoretic deterministic function [0,1]^n -> {0,1} is measurable on every possible input space.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source uses P_i(X), calibration events, and expected strategy accuracy while allowing an arbitrary deterministic C. Those expressions need measurability and integrability on an arbitrary measurable input space.

model_conventions.checked_scope: Every partition used by the source's Lemma 8 and Proposition 9 witnesses is finite and is covered by the raw joint-law construction, including agent-dependent finite cell types.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: The checked partition construction takes a finite measurable cell map for each agent. A positive-mass cell receives true-label mass divided by total cell mass; a null cell is assigned zero.
model_conventions.unresolved_relation_to_literal_source: User-approved formalization convention: the source partition sentence is read as the finite measurable cell construction used by its proof, with zero on a null cell. The report retains this scope choice without treating arbitrary atomless partitions as an open proof obligation.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source says only 'partition'. Measurability is needed to form the events, and finiteness is needed for the checked zero-cell totalization to remain expectation-irrelevant and for the calibrated event identity to follow by a finite sum.

model_conventions.checked_scope: SourceReliableJointLaw and every source-facing Theorem 1, Proposition 7, and Proposition 9 endpoint carry [Nonempty (Fin n)]. The source-domain strategy bridge never presents the zero-agent false extension as part of the paper.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: The source's use of min over i in [n] in reliability and its existential k in [n] in non-collaboration is read as requiring at least one agent: Nonempty (Fin n).
model_conventions.unresolved_relation_to_literal_source: Maintainer-approved 2026-09-03 source reading in response to the current-protocol preflight clarification request.
model_conventions.why_needed: The paper never defines a zero-agent semantics. The earlier totalized Lean predicate was false at n = 0 merely because no Fin 0 witness exists; that implementation behavior is not a source assertion.

policy: Source-proof findings are keyed by source locations and mathematical content; Lean declaration names are navigation only and are never evidence of fidelity.
A checked finite witness may establish the source proof step that uses that finite witness, but it cannot silently close a broader arbitrary-space, atomless, or nonmeasurable source statement.
An explicit event-calibration or well-formed-expectation convention must remain visible as a model convention. It cannot be hidden by relabeling it as a literal source theorem.
The finite measurable partition and zero-cell totalization are user-approved source-reading conventions for this formalization; they remain visible in the report and are not open proof obligations.
